causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Demand at 2.30 pm was 10,323 MW which was 695 MW higher than forecast one hour prior.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: Rooftop solar output dropped from over 5,000 MW at midday to around 3,000 MW at 2.30 pm when the high prices occurred.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Calm conditions saw relatively low levels of wind output with an average of around 800 MW on the day. Wind output was even lower at the time of the high prices, averaging 587 MW during the high price period, which equates to around 20% of the installed capacity in NSW.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: An unplanned network outage on the Lower Tumut to Yass line in southern NSW also contributed to the high prices by limiting access to low-priced generation from southern NSW and Victoria.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: There was also an unplanned outage on the Muswellbrook to Tamworth line in northern NSW which prevented around 200 MW of low-priced solar generation from being dispatched.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: An unplanned outage of all three Directlink cables on the Terranora interconnector since 26 December also limited flows on the interconnector to around 18 MW into NSW.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: An unplanned outage of all three Directlink cables on the Terranora interconnector since 26 December also limited flows on the interconnector to around 18 MW into NSW.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: On this day, for one of the two high-priced 5-minute intervals, at 2.10 pm, offers of around $17,500 per MW in lower FCAS contributed to setting the energy price in NSW.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: During the high prices, around 800 MW of gas units could not start up quickly enough, and a further 800 MW from units already running could not ramp up quickly enough to mitigate the high prices.

causes.label: constraint_violation
causes.quote: For the 2.05 pm interval, this outage meant AEMO needed to back off negatively-priced generation at Snowy Hydro's Tumut Power Station, resulting in a high price (section 4.3).

interconnectors_named.name: Terranora
interconnectors_named.quote: Terranora, the remaining interconnector into Queensland, cannot transfer FCAS.

interconnectors_named.name: QNI
interconnectors_named.quote: This was due to the outage creating a credible risk of losing QNI.

intervals.quote: On this day, for one of the two high-priced 5-minute intervals, at 2.10 pm, offers of around $17,500 per MW in lower FCAS contributed to setting the energy price in NSW.
intervals.text: Two high-priced 5-minute intervals at 2.05 pm and 2.10 pm

network_outages.quote: An unplanned network outage on the Lower Tumut to Yass line in southern NSW also contributed to the high prices by limiting access to low-priced generation from southern NSW and Victoria.

peak_price.quote: On 15 January, the 30-minute price in NSW reached $5,906 per MWh at 2.30 pm.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Due to continuing high temperatures, demand was very high. Average demand during the high price periods was around 10,950 MW, compared to the quarterly average demand for this time of day of around 8,550 MW. Queensland's record demand was broken by more than 200 MW at 6 pm (30-minutes prior to high prices), when demand reached 11,258 MW.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Calm conditions saw low levels of wind output. Average wind generation for the day was relatively low at just 240 MW, compared to an average of around 350 MW across the week. During the high prices, wind output averaged 154 MW, which equates to only 7% of installed capacity in Queensland.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: Terranora was constrained by an ongoing planned outage of the Lismore SVC in NSW. To maintain system security, flows were forced into NSW, at an average of 139 MW, during the high-priced periods.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: During the high prices, QNI was flowing around 381 MW on average into Queensland, compared to its nominal capacity of 850 MW, due to a constraint in place to manage negative settlement residues (section 4.2).

causes.label: constraint_violation
causes.quote: A system normal constraint to avoid overloading network equipment in northeast Queensland also prevented an average of around 70 MW of cheap generation from being dispatched during the high prices.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Two coal units were unavailable at the time of the high prices. One of six 280 MW units at Gladstone Power Station was on an unplanned outage since the morning of 20 January, and one 443 MW unit at Tarong North Power Station was on a planned outage since 19 January. These outages meant around 700 MW of baseload capacity, most of which is typically offered at low prices, was unavailable during the high prices.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Two coal units were unavailable at the time of the high prices. These outages meant around 700 MW of baseload capacity, most of which is typically offered at low prices, was unavailable during the high prices.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding for commercial and technical reasons contributed to some of the high prices.

causes.label: battery_state_of_charge
causes.quote: Neoen shifted 192 MW of capacity from low to high prices at its Western Downs battery due to changes in its state of charge, setting the price from 6.05 pm to 6.15 pm and 7.25 pm to 7.30 pm.

causes.quote: Wind output in the regions was relatively low on the day, with an average of 1,966 MW across South Australia and Victoria, compared to an average of around 2,550 MW across the following week. At the time of the high prices, wind output averaged 1,267 MW, which equates to around 15% of installed capacity in South Australia and Victoria.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: At Snowy Hydro's Valley Power station, 47 MW was unable to be dispatched due to start-up limitations.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: At Loy Yang A Power Station, 29 MW was unable to be dispatched due to the interactions between the FCAS and energy markets (section 7.1.5).

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: AGL Energy removed 65 MW of low-priced capacity at Torrens Island B Power Station, Dalrymple North battery and Mckay power station due to plant failure

causes.label: battery_state_of_charge
causes.quote: Neoen shifted 80 MW from low to high prices in a late rebid at the Hornsdale Battery due to updated state of charge, which set the price for 7.15 pm.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Between 6.38 pm and 6.58 pm, AGL Energy removed 65 MW of low-priced capacity at Torrens Island B Power Station, Dalrymple North battery and Mckay power station due to plant failure, and shifted 142 MW of capacity from low to high prices at Barker Inlet and Torrens Island B power stations due to a change in forecast prices. These rebids contributed to the high prices at 7.05 pm and 7.10 pm, and includes a rebid of 92 MW from low to high prices at Barker Inlet Power station which set the price for both intervals.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: a system normal constraint managing transient stability on QNI for a trip of either lines from Armidale to Dumaresq or to Sapphire set the import limit on the interconnector during high-priced dispatch intervals, limiting flows into NSW to around 920 MW, compared to its nominal capacity of 1,300 MW.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: An unplanned outage of two of the three Directlink cables since 30 January limited flows into NSW on the Terranora interconnector to 100 MW out of its 210 MW nominal capacity during both high-priced dispatch intervals.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Two coal units were unavailable at the time of the high prices. One unit at Baywater Power Station and one unit at Eraring Power Station were on unplanned outages since 21 January and 3 February, respectively. These outages meant around 1,400 MW of baseload capacity, most of which is typically offered at low prices, was unavailable during the high prices.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Due to consecutive days of high daytime and evening temperatures, demand remained elevated as there was continued need for cooling. Demand during the high price period was 3,315 MW, which was the highest for the quarter and only 82 MW below the record for South Australia, set in January 2011.

AEMO's dispatch engine when considering the formulation of these constraints, determined that the least cost outcome was to back-off low-priced generation instead of dispatching higher high-priced capacity.
